pages.heading: Project Summary
lines: Redesigned the pension flow on XP’s app to improve usability, clarity, and decision-making.
Client: XP Inc. — one of the largest investment platforms in Brazil
My Role: Product Designer responsible for user research, discovery, testing, and prototyping
Platform: XP Mobile App (iOS & Android)
Timeline: 2021

pages.heading: Context
lines: Sporadic contributions are a key entry point for private pension users on XP’s mobile app. Our goal was not only to validate the usability of this new flow but also to deepen our understanding of mobile users’ behaviors, motivations, and needs around retirement investments.

pages.heading: Problem
lines: 80% of pension users did not have an active XP digital account, adding friction to the contribution journey.
Users lacked clarity on how to choose the right plan and felt unsure about taking action without an advisor.
The app’s current information architecture and available filters were insufficient to support confident decision-making.

pages.heading: Discovery & Research Strategy
lines: We launched a campaign targeting users who had shown interest in pension products via the XP product shelf. From a base of 1,000 people, 46 replied and 5 were selected for semi-structured interviews. These interviews aimed to:
Validate usability of the new sporadic contribution flow.
Understand user profiles, goals, and blockers.
Uncover the emotional drivers and rational criteria involved in retirement planning.

pages.heading: Interview Insights
lines: We interviewed 5 users across different segments and mapped them by behavior and digital maturity:
Jonnas – Disciplined | Has pension | No digital account
Rennan – Enthusiast | Has pension | No digital account
Gabriela – Dependent | Has pension | Has digital account
Edwin – Self-sufficient | Has pension | Has digital account
Jessica – Disciplined | No pension | No digital account

pages.heading: Interview Insights
lines: Additional insights:
3 users linked retirement directly to long-term goals like "retirement stability."
2 valued diversification as an investment strategy.
3 did not know how to identify the best plan for their needs.
3 valued advisor support; 2 preferred self-service.

pages.heading: Key Insights
lines: Some users found the app’s structure and content hard to navigate.
There was strong demand for a pension simulator.
Many users expected to find more contextual information and filters to support comparison.
Users without an active digital account had a longer and more confusing journey.

pages.heading: Usability Test – SUM Method
lines: We used the SUM (Single Usability Metric) framework to assess efficiency, effectiveness, and satisfaction:
Overall task success rate: 76.1%
Time-on-task improved for users with an active account.
ASQ (After Scenario Questionnaire) scores averaged 7/7 for satisfaction and perceived speed.

pages.heading: Top Opportunities
lines: 1. Filters and Plan Categorization: Add more filtering options so users can compare pension plans based on relevant attributes (e.g., insurer, risk level, tax model).
2. In-Journey Educational Content: Provide better explanations during the selection process to empower users without advisors. Use benchmarks like Life Insurance journeys.
3. Simulator Campaign Integration: Leverage the WhatsApp pension simulator to support users who want autonomy but lack clarity to move forward.

pages.heading: Outcome & Next Steps
lines: Insights from this research directly informed product roadmap priorities. We:
Improved navigation and categorization of funds.
Provided clearer onboarding for users without digital accounts.
Strengthened educational layers and content touchpoints.
This project also laid the groundwork for subsequent mobile flows (e.g., Initial Contribution, Monthly Contribution, and Withdrawals), following the same logic validated here.

pages.heading: Reflection
lines: Designing for retirement in a mobile-first context revealed how emotional and behavioral variables shape financial decision-making. The work reminded us that even tech-savvy users often seek reassurance, and that good design means building confidence just as much as functionality.
